historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly rejects OS-only automation and assigns physical validation to an operator, but does not define the CPU/TPM identity, SPI transaction, electrical/timing acceptance or preservation of TPM security state.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds calibrated capture or equivalent TPM diagnostic, endpoint and probe mapping, decoded handshake evidence, TPM state protection and vendor recovery.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-01/03 require the method to prove the physical CPU-QSPI1/TPM path; ED-07/08 require endpoint-bound evidence; ED-11/12 forbid unsafe stimulus/retry; ED-36/38 retain engineer verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate functional SPI communication between the CPU's QSPI1 controller and the intended TPM without changing TPM ownership, hierarchy, PCR, NV, provisioning, firmware or trust state.
original_method: A qualified operator binds the board/CPU/TPM identities and exact QSPI1 probe points, records baseline TPM security/presence state, applies only approved high-impedance passive instrumentation or a vendor-authenticated non-mutating TPM diagnostic, captures a complete CPU-to-TPM command/response transaction with chip-select, clock/data, mode and timing, correlates it with platform logs, then removes probes and confirms unchanged TPM state; stop without TPM commands that clear, provision, write NV, extend PCRs, update firmware or reset ownership.
manual_activity: A qualified operator/vendor safely attaches calibrated high-impedance probes to approved CPU-QSPI1/TPM points, captures and decodes a non-mutating TPM exchange, documents the setup and removes the probes; or runs an approved equivalent TPM firmware diagnostic.
required_inputs: Exact CPU, TPM part/instance, board revision, QSPI1 schematic and approved probe points
SPI voltage, mode, clock, chip-select, non-mutating command/response and timing oracle
TPM baseline/postcheck for presence, health, ownership/hierarchies, PCR/NV/provisioning and firmware state
Calibrated instrument or signed diagnostic, safe probe procedure, abort limits and vendor recovery
safety_requirements: Use high-impedance passive measurement only on approved QSPI1 points; never drive or short the CPU/TPM bus
Choose a transaction proven non-mutating and preserve TPM ownership, endorsement/storage hierarchies, PCRs, NV indices, provisioning and firmware
Do not clear, take ownership, provision, write NV, extend PCRs, update firmware, reset the TPM or clear logs
Stop on unexpected security-state delta, unsafe probe loading, malformed/unknown transaction, TPM/CPU fault or boot/trust impact
No automatic repeat, reset or recovery action
agent_execution_scope: Verify CPU/TPM identities, QSPI1 mapping, safe transaction oracle, instrument calibration and immutable TPM baseline
Guide operator/vendor capture and correlate decoded command/response with the named TPM and logs
Confirm post-capture TPM security/presence state equals baseline
Do not substitute OS enumeration, attach probes, issue TPM state-changing commands, reset hardware or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CPU/TPM/QSPI1 identities, probe map, electrical/protocol/timing criteria and non-mutating exchange
Approve TPM state baseline/postcheck, operator/instrument or diagnostic procedure, aborts and recovery
Review the endpoint-bound waveform/diagnostic and unchanged-security-state evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The operator scope/handshake method fits the physical QSPI1 purpose. Generic `tpm2_getcap` or device enumeration can support identity/baseline evidence but cannot replace physical bus proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Qualified operator passively captures an approved non-mutating CPU-QSPI1/TPM exchange, or vendor runs a documented equivalent diagnostic, while recording before/after TPM security state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CPU QSPI1-to-TPM scope, AI_VR_SPI_CPU_and_TPM bundle and 10/10-minute allocation remain; device, transaction and limits are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH MANUAL CPU-QSPI1-TO-TPM FUNCTIONAL, ELECTRICAL AND STATE-PRESERVATION CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Combine calibrated passive capture of a known non-mutating TPM command/response with identity-bound decoded frames and before/after TPM trust-state evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit TPM state immutability, safe transaction selection, protocol/electrical oracle, raw capture retention and vendor recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: OS TPM presence can succeed via cached or higher-layer state without proving the physical QSPI1 waveform; conversely an arbitrary TPM command may change security state and invalidate later tests.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: TPM is part of the platform trust boundary; mis-probing, clearing, provisioning, PCR/NV operations or firmware/reset actions can affect measured boot, secrets and system recoverability.

project_override_considerations: A vendor diagnostic is equivalent only when it proves the named CPU-QSPI1-to-TPM transaction and is documented as non-mutating. OS-visible TPM inventory remains supporting evidence, not physical-link evidence.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization, board/CPU/TPM identities and QSPI1 schematic/probe map
Instrument serial/calibration/settings and setup photos, or signed diagnostic version/hash and coverage
Complete raw waveform and decoded chip-select/clock/command/response/timing, or equivalent signed diagnostic output
Before/after TPM presence, health, firmware and security-state comparison showing no unapproved mutation
CPU/TPM/BMC/boot/security logs and restored probe-free known-good state

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2165 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00052-V002: approve CPU/TPM identities and QSPI1 probe map; voltage, SPI mode, clock/chip-select, non-mutating command/response and timing limits; TPM ownership/hierarchy/PCR/NV/provisioning/firmware baseline and postcheck; calibrated instrument or equivalent signed diagnostic; safe procedure, aborts, and recovery.

review_improvement: Requires actual endpoint-bound QSPI1 evidence while explicitly preserving the TPM trust state, preventing a physical-link test from clearing or reprovisioning a security device.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row is not satisfied by seeing `/dev/tpm*`: the source names the physical CPU QSPI1 link. The evidence must therefore show a transaction whose chip select and decoded response belong to the target TPM. Unlike an ordinary peripheral, TPM operations can mutate ownership, PCR or NV state and affect measured boot and secrets. A preapproved non-mutating exchange plus before/after trust-state comparison is essential, and the physical probe work keeps the case MANUAL ONLY.
